_comment: A foot block squares the turn it made onto riders inside its ranks once they are gone, without an order (#1859). A 48-man Infantry block (8 files by 6 ranks) stands on Hold facing east, and a brittle 12-horse Cavalry troop (morale 3) charges it from the north-east, rides into its ranks, breaks and flees south. While the riders are inside the block, each small re-face onto them is folded into the formation (#1792), so the men turn to face them where they stand and the ranks do not wheel round after them: by tick 680, still in contact, the ranks stand 64.5 degrees off the block's heading (36.9 to 64.5 over the clip seed and perturbed seeds 1 to 4). On main f12d083f that fold then stays for as long as the block gets no order: at tick 900, three and a half seconds after the block left contact (ticks 684 to 710 by seed), it still reads 64.5 degrees (57.1, 61.6, 57.6, 36.9 on seeds 1 to 4). Now the turn made onto the riders is squared on its own once the block is out of contact, no faster than the men on the far corners can jog: it is done by tick 820 to 884 by seed, and at tick 900 the ranks read 0.1 to 0.3 degrees off the heading on all five seeds. The tick-900 claim's 1-degree tolerance covers the dump's rounding, which keeps a square grid from reading exactly 0: the heading is written to 2 decimals (up to about 0.4 degrees on its own) and the grid's front to 4. The tick-680 check (50 +/- 15 degrees) only shows the fold is there to square and passes on both trees; the tick-8 position, tick-360 Hold, tick-440 FIGHTING and tick-720 ROUTING checks are setup, also passing on both, and tick 900 still reads Hold, so no order squared it. The clip ends at tick 900, before the troop rallies (tick 918 on the clip seed, 886 on perturbed seed 4), since a rallying troop's re-form is not what this clip shows. Static camera. Deterministic (scenario + seed + scripted input). Measured with full state dumps every 2 ticks on main f12d083f and on the #1859 change (Windows). Re-pinned 2026-11-04 on e58a15a9, where a cavalry troop in contact wheels onto its enemy at a bounded rate instead of snapping (#1806), measured with full state dumps every 2 ticks on seeds 0 to 4 against main d0272c6d. The riders now stay inside the block longer: it last touches them at ticks 716, 738, 714 and 726 on seeds 0 to 3 (684, 708, 692 and 706 on main; seed 4 plays as on main, 682). At tick 680 the ranks stand 74.6, 58.7, 73.6, 70.4 and 36.9 degrees off the heading (main: 64.5, 57.1, 61.6, 57.6, 36.9), so that check now reads 56 +/- 20, spanning the five seeds as the 50 +/- 15 it replaces spanned main's. The squaring itself is unchanged, about 200 ticks at the bounded rate with no order, but it starts later and finishes at ticks 918, 916, 914 and 922 (870 to 884 on main, 820 on seed 4), after tick 900, where the ranks still read 4.0, 3.3, 3.1 and 4.8 degrees off. So the square check and the Hold check that goes with it move from tick 900 to tick 940, where the ranks read 0.1 to 0.3 degrees off on every seed on both trees, with the same 1-degree tolerance. The troop rallies at tick 918 (886 on seed 4), so the clip now runs past its rally.

shape_residual.reason: Uid 0 (the infantry block), shape_residual: Dense 2-tick FULL dumps, every exemption removed, Windows, seeds 0 to 4, measured 2026-11-04: d0272c6d passes on every seed; e58a15a9 (a cavalry block in contact wheels at a bounded rate, #1806) reads 28.56, 29.82, 24.98, pass and pass against 13.5. Traced on seed 0: the riders now wheel inside and beside the block instead of snapping, so they leave contact later (tick 716 against 684), and at tick 680 the block's grid is fitted 30.6 degrees off its men (2.0 on main). Which re-face put it there is not traced; a foot block's small re-face in contact, unlike a cavalry block's, still snaps (#1806). The residual is judged out of contact, while the men walk back onto the squaring grid.
